scope: Proposition 2.6 (Thermodynamic limits and duality) of the manuscript “A radial continuum phase transition with algebraic decay” (preprints/A-radial-continuum-phase-transition-with-algebraic-decay-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 228 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d53cafa68c322a07), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every member φ of (2.2), including countably infinite sums, and every β > 0, d ≥ 0, the limit Hφ(β, d) = lim L→∞ n/L3→d Hφ L,n(β) (2.12) exists along every such sequence of real sides and integer counts. It is finite, convex and continuous in d ∈ [0, ∞), and concave in β > 0 for each fixed d. The bounds (2.10) hold with Hφ(β, d) and d in place of their finite volume counterparts. The grand partition function and pressure satisfy Ξφ L(β, h) = X n≥0 ethn Zφ L,n(β), Qφ(β, h) = lim L→∞ log Ξφ L(β, h) tL3 . (2.13) The pressure is finite, nonnegative, and jointly convex on Ω. For β > 0, Qφ(β, h) = sup d≥0 {hd − Hφ(β, d)}, Hφ(β, d) = sup h∈R {hd − Qφ(β, h)}, d > 0. (2.14) For fixed admissible t, pressures of the whole family are uniformly bounded on each compact subset of Ω.
